notes.question: JustVugg's question on #2264 (2026-10-22): DSV4_MM_WARP is on by default (auto) in PR #1's mm_batch, so it changes the prefill of every FP8 checkpoint on a generic CUDA build, not only the COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH=1 path the earlier manifests measured; measure the default configuration (no COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH) on the full V4 Flash, dev against the branch, prompt and decode, interleaved. It stays on by default if bit-identical and not slower. The point of this manifest is therefore 'not slower, bit-identical', not a speed-up: in the default configuration the prefill MoE runs on the CPU union in both arms, and the warp kernel only takes the batched attention's short fp8 rows. On a DeepGEMM build DSV4_MM_WARP and DSV4_MOE_EXPERT_MAJOR are compiled out (#ifndef COLI_DSV4_DEEPGEMM), so this checks that the rest of PR #1 leaves the DeepGEMM path's texts and speed alone.
